answer: Each agent must escrow a scarce token and earn a trust score only through transactions that counterparties later confirm; repeated trades among linked accounts count as one relationship, not many. To extract value, an attacker must fund many independent escrows and persuade unrelated agents to accept and verify them, tying up capital and risking slashing for false confirmations. An ocean of identities therefore cannot cheaply manufacture reputation: a fable about free trust dissolves under the quartz-like cost of locked collateral.
